_comment: Task B2 (Bunyamin). Safe haven and science stops for the Bright Angel EVA. Positions are Perseverance end-of-drive localizations from M20_waypoints.json (Mars 2000 sphere, lon east-positive); pipeline A4 converts them to AOI metres. Each position is the rover's location on arrival, within a few tens of metres of the outcrop, not the outcrop itself. Stop order is the rover's visiting order.
source: NASA/JPL-Caltech Mars 2020 MMGIS layer M20_waypoints.json; sols matched to targets from the NASA pages in each source_url

safe_haven.name: Safe haven (pressurized rover)
safe_haven.why: A spot where Perseverance itself parked on the Margin unit before entering Neretva Vallis. The rover measured 4.5° tilt here, below the 15° caution slope. All five stops are 0.4-1.1 km away, so the planned walk fits the 360 min budget with the 60 min reserve intact (rough estimate). Slope from the DEM is still to be checked when A3 publishes slope_2m.
safe_haven.flag: Position chosen by us (Assumed as a parking site); flatness from rover tilt only, not yet from the 2 m slope raster.

stops.name: Mount Washburn
stops.why: A hill of boulders with textures and compositions never seen before on Mars; the first science stop inside Neretva Vallis, reached after a 200 m drive in one sol.

stops.name: Tuff Cliff
stops.why: Outcrop 132 m north of Mount Washburn; the lowest member of the lake-deposited Tuff Cliff to Walhalla Glades succession of the Bright Angel formation.

stops.name: Bright Angel
stops.why: Light-toned outcrops at the northern edge of the channel, reached on June 9, 2024 after a four-sol, 605 m drive; the type area of the Bright Angel formation.

stops.name: Cheyava Falls
stops.why: The rock with the 'leopard spots' and the Sapphire Canyon core (collected July 21, 2024, about sol 1215): the potential biosignature a human geologist would come to check. Rover arrived at this workspace on sol 1210.

stops.name: Masonic Temple
stops.why: Strata on the southern margin of Neretva Vallis with rocks like Bright Angel's (Hurowitz et al. 2025, Nature); a comparison site, abrasion target Malgosa Crest on sol 1242. Rover position from sol 1231 to 1244.
stops.flag: Position inferred: no NASA news page names the sol; matched from the Malgosa Crest abrasion sol (1242) in Hurowitz et al. 2025 to the rover's parking spot over sols 1231-1244.
